experiences.title: Jungle Safari — Dhela & Jhirna Zones
experiences.description: A visit to Jim Corbett is incomplete without experiencing the thrill of a jungle safari. Corbett Foothills Retreat offers privileged access to the Dhela and Jhirna safari zones — two of the park's most biodiverse and tiger-rich ranges. Dhela, the newest tourism zone, is known for its open grasslands and high density of Bengal tiger sightings, while Jhirna offers year-round access with lush sal forests, sparkling streams, and abundant populations of elephants, wild boars, spotted deer, and sloth bears. Both zones provide exceptional birdwatching with over 600 avian species including crested serpent eagles, great hornbills, and kingfishers. Our expert naturalists accompany every safari, sharing deep knowledge of animal behaviour, tracking techniques, and the unique ecology of each zone.
highlights: Dhela Zone: Open grasslands, high tiger density, excellent for photography
Jhirna Zone: Year-round access, sal forests, elephants and sloth bears
Expert naturalist guides with deep knowledge of animal behaviour and tracking
Over 600 bird species including crested serpent eagles and great hornbills
Canter & gypsy safaris available with flexible timing options
Located only 8 km from the retreat

experiences.title: Guided Wilderness Walks
experiences.description: Step beyond the safari vehicle and immerse yourself in the jungle on foot with our expert-led wilderness walks. These guided interpretive treks take you through the forest fringe, riverine trails, and village pathways that border the Corbett landscape. Led by trained naturalists, each walk reveals the hidden world of animal tracks, medicinal plants, edible forest produce, and the intricate web of life that sustains the wilderness. Guests learn to identify pugmarks, distinguish bird calls, recognize native tree species like sal, khair, and semal, and understand the ancient bond between local communities and the forest. These walks are tailored to all fitness levels — from gentle morning strolls to more immersive half-day expeditions.
highlights: Expert-led interpretive treks through forest fringe and riverine trails
Learn to identify animal tracks, pugmarks, and bird calls
Discover medicinal plants, native tree species, and edible forest produce
Tailored to all fitness levels — gentle strolls to half-day expeditions
Morning and twilight walks available
Photography-friendly itineraries with naturalist guidance

experiences.title: Bird Watching
experiences.description: The forests and surrounding habitats of Jim Corbett are a paradise for bird enthusiasts. The region is home to hundreds of resident and migratory bird species, making it one of North India's most rewarding birdwatching destinations. Early mornings are particularly magical, with the sounds of birds echoing through the forest canopy. Guests may encounter kingfishers, woodpeckers, hornbills, barbets, eagles, and numerous other species depending on the season. Whether you are an experienced birder or a curious beginner, birdwatching around the retreat is a peaceful and rewarding experience.
highlights: Ideal for bird enthusiasts and wildlife photographers
Great for families with children and nature lovers
Hundreds of resident and migratory bird species

experiences.title: Late-Night Riverside Bonfire
experiences.description: As darkness settles over the jungle and the stars emerge above the Kosi riverbed, gather around a crackling bonfire for an evening of storytelling, stargazing, and soulful connection. Our late-night riverside bonfire gatherings are a signature Corbett Foothills Retreat experience — the perfect antidote to city life. Seated on traditional earthen diyas-lit grounds with the sound of the river flowing nearby, guests share tales of the day's wildlife encounters, toast marshmallows under the open sky, and listen to folk tales of the Kumaon hills narrated by local village elders. The experience includes freshly brewed chai, locally sourced snacks, and the warm glow of a fire that mirrors the hospitality of the retreat itself.
highlights: Riverside location along the Kosi riverbed under a canopy of stars
Traditional earthen diya-lit seating creating an intimate ambience
Local Kumaoni folk tales narrated by village elders
Freshly brewed chai and locally sourced snacks by the fire
Stargazing opportunities in the pristine night sky
Perfect for families, couples, and solo travelers

about.tagline: Where personalized hospitality meets the untamed beauty of the forest
paragraphs: Nestled at the edge of the legendary Jim Corbett Forest, Corbett Foothills Retreat is not merely a destination — it is a thoughtfully curated sanctuary for travelers seeking authenticity, tranquility, and meaningful connection with nature. Conceived around a bespoke hospitality philosophy, the retreat offers an experience that is both intimate and deeply personal, where every stay is shaped by genuine care, attentive service, and an unwavering commitment to guest comfort.

Unlike large commercial resorts where guests often become just another room number, Corbett Foothills Retreat is a boutique farmstay with only six exclusive suites. This intentionally intimate scale allows the hosts to devote individual attention to every guest, understanding their unique preferences and creating experiences tailored to their needs.

Positioned in a privileged forest-edge location adjoining the wilderness of Corbett, the retreat offers uninterrupted views, pristine air, and a rare opportunity to experience nature in its purest form. Here, the rhythm of life slows down. Mornings begin with birdsong instead of traffic, evenings unfold beneath starlit skies, and the constant urgency of city life gradually gives way to a more mindful and restorative pace.

A deep commitment to organic farming and sustainable living lies at the heart of the retreat's ethos. The property embraces responsible stewardship of the land through eco-conscious practices and farm-to-table experiences that celebrate freshness, seasonality, and local produce.

Seamlessly balancing wilderness with comfort, Corbett Foothills Retreat offers contemporary conveniences thoughtfully integrated into the surrounding landscape. Every element has been designed to preserve the serenity of the environment while providing the warmth and refinement expected by modern travelers.

ecoPractices.title: Traditional Earthen Seating
ecoPractices.description: Our common areas feature handcrafted earthen seating inspired by traditional Kumaoni village architecture. These mud-and-lime plastered platforms, known locally as 'chaukis', are naturally cool in summer, warm in winter, and represent our commitment to indigenous craftsmanship and low-impact design.

ecoPractices.title: Zero Plastic Footprint
ecoPractices.description: We have eliminated single-use plastics entirely from our operations. Glass water bottles are refilled from our own RO filtration system, toiletries are dispensed in refillable ceramic containers, and all packaging is compostable or recyclable. Guests receive jute tote bags for their safari essentials.

ecoPractices.title: Solar-Powered Operations
ecoPractices.description: The retreat runs on a hybrid solar power system that meets the majority of our energy needs. Solar water heaters serve all guest bathrooms, and energy-efficient LED lighting illuminates the property. We offset remaining consumption through tree-planting initiatives within the local community.

ecoPractices.title: Farm-to-Table Dining
ecoPractices.description: Our kitchen garden supplies seasonal vegetables, herbs, and spices that feature in every meal. Guests can walk through the gardens, pick their own produce, and watch as our chefs transform it into authentic Kumaoni cuisine. Nothing is wasted — organic waste is composted back into the soil.

ecoPractices.title: Rainwater Harvesting
ecoPractices.description: A comprehensive rainwater harvesting system captures monsoon runoff from every rooftop, replenishing the groundwater table and sustaining our irrigation needs throughout the dry months. The property also features a natural wastewater treatment pond that supports local biodiversity.

ecoPractices.title: Local Community Engagement
ecoPractices.description: We employ exclusively from nearby villages, source supplies from local artisans and farmers, and support village schools through our guest donation programme. Our guided walks often include visits to neighbouring hamlets where guests interact with families preserving centuries-old Kumaoni traditions.
